summary: Ephemeral LB session-token reuse during websocket handoff duplicates stream metadata and drops terminal tokens
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent websocket sessions where, after an LB-induced connection handoff, the resumed stream contains duplicated metadata control frames (choice/metadata events repeated) and is missing the final terminal tokens for the last choice. This leads to downstream parsers seeing duplicate 'choice' blocks followed by a truncated final sentence.

Impact:
- Production traffic for a small set of enterprise customers experiences incomplete final output in ~0.2% of streams for long responses (>2k tokens).
- Downstream consumer logic de-duplicates metadata, which in some cases causes the last choice to be discarded entirely (customer-visible content loss).
- Customer has reported user-facing failures in a document-generation flow (FinSight Analytics) and is requesting urgency.

Environment:
- Prod, us-east region behind CloudFront -> NGINX LB (ephemeral connections enabled) -> websocket-proxy -> api-gateway -> serving-runtime.
- Customer traffic uses pinned model redwood-gemini-xt-1.2 and fallback to open-llama-13b-q4.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Start a long streaming generation (seeded prompt that produces ~3k tokens).
2) Force an LB connection flip (reproduce by toggling health check to trigger connection migration on the WB proxy or briefly cut TCP).
3) Client reconnects with existing session-token and resumes.
4) Server emits continuation events plus a small set of metadata/choice control frames; during some handoffs the client receives duplicate metadata frames followed by an abrupt end-of-stream with no terminal tokens.

Observed logs / snippets (redacted):
- websocket-proxy logs around handoff: "Handoff sessionToken=abc123 -> reused on new conn; old_conn_fd closed"
- api-gateway: "resume_request sessionToken=abc123 offset=2350"
- serving-runtime trace: "resume: emitted continuation chunk id=0..4; flushed meta-frame:choice-start" then "meta-frame:choice-start" (duplicate) then "EOS without terminal-token"

Initial investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: session-token reuse + non-idempotent resume path causes the serving-runtime to send both a leftover buffered meta frame and a fresh meta frame after reconnection (duplicate).
- Hypothesis 2: a race during handshake makes the gateway interpret the reconnection as a fresh session and also replay the tail of the old stream leading to overlapping fragments and truncated terminal tokens.
- Reproducible in canary when artificially inducing LB flips; rate is low and depends on exact timing of KV cache flush and handshake completion.
- Correlated with specific LB configuration that uses short keepalive and immediate connection teardown (NGINX proxy_running_v1.14 with upstream keepalive=1).

Immediate mitigation proposed:
- Add defensive deduplication in websocket-proxy: drop immediate back-to-back identical meta frames within X ms for the same session-token.
- Add a small grace window on resume to wait for any outstanding frames from previous connection (100ms) before sending fresh metadata.
- Customer workaround: enable short-term non-strict resume on client (client-side ignore exact duplicate meta frames) while we deploy server fix.

Next steps:
- SRE to reproduce reliably in staging with LB flip harness (assigned).
- Serving runtime team to add logging around resume idempotency (PR reference in linked PRs).
- Engineering to test metadata dedupe patch on websocket-proxy in canary for 48h before wider rollout.

Expected ETA for hotfix deployment: 2026-03-15 if tests pass.

Please see related PRs and runbook link for more artifacts.
investigation_notes: Recreated locally with LB flip script; observed duplicate meta frames in pcap and runtime traces. KV cache eviction window aligns with race where both old connection flush and new resume send meta frames. Running an instrumented build of websocket-proxy (branch: ws-resume-dedupe) with 50ms suppress window eliminated duplicates in 200/200 test runs. Need further canary and backward-compat checks for heartbeat and multiplexed sessions.
resolution_notes: Patch prepared for websocket-proxy to suppress identical metadata frames within a 100ms window for the same session-token (PR #4821). Serving-runtime will add a resume token monotonic counter to avoid replaying the same metadata frame (PR #4839). Planning canary deploy 2026-03-13; post-canary rollout if no regressions. Customer notified of workaround and will enable client-side dedupe in the interim.
